subject: Post-call: hosted fit — latency verification & streaming concurrency asks
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: hosted fit — latency verification & streaming concurrency asks

Alex / Sanjay — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a proposed set of next steps so we can validate fit against your p95/p99 goals. TL;DR: we think Hosted can meet your e2e SLOs with a short canary + traffic-shaped probe; below are the numbers we heard and what we’ll test.

What we captured on the call (please correct if anything is off):
- Current provider (incumbent) measured on your production traffic: p95 ≈ 920 ms, p99 ≈ 2.6 s (tail-heavy during convo bursts).
- Target for mission-critical endpoint: p95 <= 350 ms, p99 <= 1.1 s (these are your stated goals for end-to-end requests including client-side wiring and streaming).
- Streaming behavior: client-side uses chunked SSE streaming, typical response lengths 40–120 tokens, median 60 tokens; you need first-chunk latency <= 150 ms 95% of the time for a good UX.
- Throughput/traffic envelope for the pilot: sustained 45–60 RPS with 180 concurrent open streaming connections during peak, burst to 200 RPS for short windows.
- Important constraints: cannot increase client-side request timeouts (60s), and any fallback path must preserve ordered partial results.

What Redwood will validate in the canary/probe:
1) End-to-end p95/p99 on realistic traffic replay (we’ll run your trace with identical concurrency and token mix). Target verification: p95 <= 350 ms, p99 <= 1.1 s.
2) First-chunk latency distribution for streaming: p95 <= 150 ms, p99 <= 450 ms.
3) Throughput and open-connection stability: sustain 60 RPS with 180 open streaming sessions for 30 minutes without queueing/backpressure events.
4) Failure/fallback behavior: exercise model-variant fallback and region failover to verify graceful degradation and consistent partial results.

Immediate asks from your side (items we agreed on):
- Provide a 10-minute production trace (anonymized) for a representative endpoint (attachment: trace-sample-1.jsonl / small-sample).
- Confirm traffic window dates for a 2-hour canary and a 30-minute ramp test.
- If possible, share any client-side timeout or SDK instrumentation that changes network timing.

Attached: perf-metrics-postcall.csv (summary rows you referenced) and trace-sample-1.jsonl (sanitized excerpt).

Proposed next steps / schedule:
- You: share full 10-min trace + confirm 2-hour canary window by EOD Wed (3/16).
- Us: prepare a paired replay harness and a pre-configured canary model variant; we’ll sketch the test runbook and share by Thu (3/17).
- Joint: run canary week of 3/21 (flexible).

Ben / Rishi — I’m looping you in to help scope the replay harness and the metrics we’ll collect (traces, per-token timing, connection-level events).

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0162
Redwood Inference

Attachments: perf-metrics-postcall.csv (CSV, 12KB), trace-sample-1.jsonl (JSONL, 58KB)

From: Alex Chen <alex@veridian.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: hosted fit — latency verification & streaming concurrency asks

Camila — thanks for the clear recap. Quick corrections and additions inline: 

> Current provider measured on your production traffic: p95 ≈ 920 ms, p99 ≈ 2.6 s
This is accurate for the endpoint we discussed (regression retrieval + prompt expansion). Note that during our weekly digest batch (not part of the pilot) p99 spikes above 4s but that’s out-of-scope.

> Target for mission-critical endpoint: p95 <= 350 ms, p99 <= 1.1 s
Those are the product targets we’d like to achieve; engineering will accept a staged approach (p95 first, then p99 improvement) if we can demonstrate consistent first-chunk streaming latency.

Additional notes:
- We can provide the anonymized trace by tomorrow morning (3/15). Will include a short README that maps request ids to features.
- Our SDK currently batches tokens client-side in 20ms windows occasionally — that may influence first-chunk timing. I’ll note that in the README.
- Canary windows: preferred days Tue/Wed next week (3/22–3/23) morning PST.

Two asks for Redwood engineers:
1) Can you confirm whether the hosted runtime will preserve SSE chunk ordering during model-variant fallback? We have strict ordering guarantees in our client.
2) For the replay harness, can you run a control pass with the incumbent’s exported traces so we can compare side-by-side?

Thanks — Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex@veridian.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: hosted fit — latency verification & streaming concurrency asks

Alex / Team — appreciate the quick turnaround on the trace. A couple of operational clarifications from our side and a concrete canary proposal: 

Operational clarifications:
- SSE chunk ordering: Redwood’s hosted streaming preserves chunk order end-to-end within a single connection; when a region-model fallback occurs we maintain an ordered merge for partials — we’ll capture sequence ids on the client to validate. Rishi, please add the ordering test to the runbook.
- Control pass: we can replay the trace against both Redwood-hosted and the incumbent instance your trace used (we’ll need a short access token/endpoint for the incumbent replay).

Canary proposal (concrete):
- Setup: 2-hour canary (90 minutes steady ramp, 30 minutes burst window) on Tue 2027-03-23 09:00–11:00 PST.
- Traffic: replay your 10-minute trace looped with concurrency set to 180 open streaming sessions, target sustained 60 RPS, short burst to 200 RPS at minute 90.
- Measurements we’ll publish: per-request p50/p95/p99, first-chunk latency distribution, backpressure events, token throughput, per-connection error rates.
- Artifacts we’ll share: consolidated replay logs (jsonl), per-token timing histogram, Grafana dashboard link, and a short decision memo (pass / fail / caveats).

Logistics:
- Alex — please confirm the incumbent endpoint and provide the anonymized trace by EOD Mon (3/15).
- Camila — I’ll own the runbook and coordinate the run with Rishi and infra on our side.
- HubSpot: I’ve attached the test plan draft and created HS record VER-2027-031; link is in metadata.

If that schedule works I’ll reserve the canary slot and prep a Doc with the replay instructions.

Ben

--
